first.rationale: The concurrent declines in onboarding completion and activation make onboarding simplification the most direct durable-revenue intervention. Prior evidence indicates it improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption, while promotional pricing may address competitive pressure but has documented 30-day retention harm. Verify both the onboarding result and the pricing trade-off before committing.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. Verified evidence shows shortened onboarding increased completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%; inherited evidence also supports a durable first-week activation lift from reducing signup fields. This directly addresses both current declines and supports sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: despite acquisition and near-term qualified-revenue lift, verified evidence shows 30-day retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive its first renewal cycle.

final2.rationale: Maintain the onboarding-simplification experiment. It directly addresses the observed declines in onboarding completion and activation and has verified evidence of higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention. The competitor's price cut creates an acute SMB risk, but the only inherited pricing evidence shows that targeted discounting raises short-term qualified revenue while reducing 30-day retention by 12% and failing before first renewal. Escalate the SMB churn signal operationally, but do not spend this experiment slot on a response with documented downstream value destruction.
